Consider the region bounded by the curve $x={e}^{y},$ the vertical line $x=e,$ and the horizontal line $y=0,$ as shown in the picture. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=e.$
question.worked_solution:
We want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curve and the line $x=e$ by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y} & =e \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=1$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/93fd0875ea2ba1d1d92bb781a61cfb114ac88b7d240cd825b4842f686f7c760f.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x={e}^{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=e.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(e)-({e}^{y})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[e-{e}^{y}]}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{2}-2{e}^{y+1}+{e}^{2y})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi ({e}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}y-2{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{y+1}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{2y}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\pi ({e}^{2}y\,{|}_{0}^{1}-2{e}^{y+1}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{{e}^{2y}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =\pi (({e}^{2}-0)-2({e}^{2}-e)+(\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =\pi (-{e}^{2}+2e+\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{(4e-{e}^{2}-1)\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}(-1+4e-{e}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
